title: Runway Briefing: United's Stranded Seats, Delta's Hawaii Whiplash, and JetBlue Buys Its Way Into LaGuardia
summary: United bought hundreds of fancy lie-flat seats for a plane that still doesn't exist, and now they might not even fit. Delta can't decide if it wants to fly to Hawaii or not. Plus, JetBlue pays nearly sixty million bucks for old Spirit slots, and United's new app feature quietly makes life miserable for airline employees flying standby.
